characters.name: Pearl Casey
characters.arc:
protagonist — wants to prove her worth beyond her father’s shadow —  — — age: 29
Active Arc: In Chapter 8, Pearl deliberately lets herself be followed into the subway tunnels to trap the saboteur, driving the action by sacrificing her safety rather than waiting for backup.
characters.voice: sharp, clipped, uses humor as armor

characters.name: Sergeant Michael Doyle
characters.arc:
ally/NYPD — wants to keep his precinct clean but is bound by bureaucracy —  — — age: 45
Active Arc: In Chapter 11, Doyle bypasses orders to protect Pearl from a corrupt captain, actively choosing loyalty over career survival.
characters.voice: weary, gravelly, uses Irish lilt sparingly

characters.name: Silas Vane
characters.arc:
antagonist/Industrialist — wants to monopolize transit contracts —  — — age: 52
Active Arc: In Chapter 6, Vane invites Pearl to tea, not to interrogate her, but to offer her a bribe, attempting to co-opt her investigation through wealth rather than violence.

characters.name: Lao Wei
characters.arc:
Chinatown apothecary — wants to protect his community from gang violence —  — — age: 60
Active Arc: In Chapter 9, Wei refuses to give Pearl the antidote for the poison found on the victim until she agrees to burn the evidence linking his son to the crime, driving the moral conflict.

characters.name: Elena Rossi
characters.arc:
immigrant seamstress — wants to feed her children —  — — age: 34
Active Arc: In Chapter 4, Elena confronts Pearl about searching her home, physically blocking the doorway until Pearl proves she isn’t there for arrest, shifting the power dynamic.

settings.name: The East River Dockyards
settings.description: smell of rotting fish and coal smoke, sound of lapping black water against rotting pilings.

settings.name: Vane’s Fifth Avenue Townhouse
settings.description: smell of beeswax and expensive tobacco, sound of a grand piano practicing scales in the next room.

settings.name: The Bowery Tenement
settings.description: smell of boiled cabbage and unwashed bodies, sound of coughing echoing through thin walls.

settings.name: Chinatown Apothecary
settings.description: smell of dried ginseng and opium, sound of rain drumming on tin roof.

plot_points.description: Pearl finds the key sewn into the victim’s hem — establishes the mystery.
Elena warns Pearl about "men in grey coats" watching the tenements.
Pearl realizes the key belongs to Vane’s private office, not the factory.
Wei reveals the victim was poisoned, not just drowned, changing the motive.
Pearl confronts Vane on the railway rooftop; he tries to push her off.
Pearl burns the ledger, saving the workers but losing the legal proof.

themes: the invisibility of women in law enforcement
voice: Close third, past tense, lean and tactile with a dry, period-appropriate wit that favors concrete observation over emotional exposition.
